assertions.name: hfree_holds_c_free_equals_2A
assertions.source: orbit count of the q=1 shadow of atom_braid_word_3A(include_inter=False), over 228 (Z,N) pairs with A = 2..20. The free word is A disjoint 3-strand blocks, each leaving 2 orbits, so 3A - A = 2A.

assertions.name: hmerge_holds_c_free_minus_c_atom_equals_A_minus_1
assertions.source: orbit count of the q=1 shadow with include_inter=True, against A+1. This is ClassicalTraceFloor's hmerge, re-derived from the live producer rather than from the recorded A = 2..20 table.

assertions.name: every_interface_letter_joins_two_DISTINCT_cycles
assertions.source: the mechanism, checked letter by letter: at the moment each interface letter s_g is applied, g and g+1 lie in DIFFERENT cycles of the partial product, so the letter merges rather than splits. Exactly the not-SameCycle hypothesis of QOU.MassTheory.orbitDefect_swap_mul_of_not_sameCycle, and the reason A-1 applications of it give hmerge. A single splitting interface would break the count; there are none.

assertions.name: no_float_field_of_the_word_was_ever_read
assertions.source: the NO-FLOAT64 guard, made mechanical rather than asserted in prose. Each letter of atom_braid_word_3A is (c, d, g); c and d carry h = q - q^-1 and are the only float-bearing fields. This records every tuple position the probe touched, and checks each g is a Python int. A future edit that starts reading c or d to build the shadow trips this instead of silently putting float64 arithmetic underneath a q=1 statement -- which is the whole reason the q=1 shadow is well defined here (at q=1, h=0, so every d template vanishes and only g survives).

assertions.name: classical_limit_restatement_NOT_an_independent_check
assertions.source: #6611 refutes B = Q_beta*Delta_tr and replaces it with B = E_0*log(tr_free/tr_atom). Schur-Weyl at q=1 gives tr = 2^(c-n), so log(tr_free/tr_atom) = (c_free - c_atom)*log 2, and hmerge makes that bracket A-1: the surviving law's q=1 limit is E_0*(A-1)*log 2, a pure bond count with no ansatz. READ THE NAME: given the hmerge assertion above, this one is ARITHMETIC RESTATEMENT, not independent evidence -- multiplying both sides of c_free - c_atom = A-1 by log 2 cannot fail. It is recorded so the inference is written down and auditable, NOT because it was tested. WHAT IS NOT VERIFIED HERE: the Schur-Weyl leg tr = 2^(c-n) itself. That is ClassicalTraceFloor's step 1, which that file assumes as a published theorem via the explicit hypotheses hSWfree/hSWatom because Mathlib has no Schur-Weyl duality; this probe never evaluates a Markov trace. So the chain is 'IF Schur-Weyl THEN the limit is (A-1)*log 2', and only the THEN half is measured. SHAPE ONLY -- E_0 is a calibration, not a derivation (qou-59j5), and #6611 leaves E_0's 2.656x scale gap open, so no magnitude is claimed.

description: Re-derives ClassicalTraceFloor's two stated step-2 hypotheses from the live producer and checks the MECHANISM hmerge names letter by letter: that each of the A-1 interface letters joins two DISTINCT cycles when applied. That side condition is the not-SameCycle hypothesis QOU.MassTheory.orbitDefect_swap_mul_of_not_sameCycle takes. Integer permutation data only -- c and d are never read, so no float enters a q=1 claim.

data.verdict: Both of ClassicalTraceFloor's step-2 hypotheses hold across 228 (Z,N) pairs with A = 2..20, re-derived from the live producer. The new content is the MECHANISM: every one of the A-1 interface letters joins two DISTINCT cycles at the moment it is applied, with zero exceptions -- so hmerge is exactly A-1 applications of orbitDefect_swap_mul_of_not_sameCycle, each with its not-SameCycle hypothesis met. That is what makes the Lean induction a bookkeeping exercise rather than an open question. Consequence for the SURVIVING binding law of #6611: its q=1 limit is E_0*(A-1)*log 2, a pure bond count. Shape only; no magnitude, E_0 being a calibration.
